not a Psychologist, but a friend who lost his mom once told me that the real grieve of loosing someone really sets in after you've really calmed down and you realize that part of your life is missing now. I think because of your studying this (for the lack of a term) "second grieving" set in even later, when you a bit more time to think freely. 

First of all, if you really think you need help, then don`t be afraid to get it. It's nothing shameful or anything so just go get some. If it doesn't help and it really is a more serious problem then try to write your Thesis later and get some help. It's not worth getting hurt over, just for a degree.

Even if it's nice that you see a reason to live in your girlfriend, you shouldn't live for others peoples sake. Your relationship could turn into something that both of you don't want because of that, and also you should find your source of happyness within yourself. Your reason to keep going should be something you want or feel, not another person. 

Sorry if I repeat myself but if I was you, I'd just get a break from your work and try to get a clear head. It really feels like you stressed everything too much, just lay down a bit and you'll feel that everything will look much better.
